topic_concept: Real Image Formation in Space
question_text: A student forms a sharp real image on a viewing card using a lens of f = 12 cm. When the card is taken away, what happens to the real image?
correct_answer_and_steps: The real inverted image still exists in empty space at that exact focal position (aerial image). The screen merely scatters light diffusely so observers can view it from all angles; the convergence of light rays occurs independently of the screen.
student_response: The image disappears completely because an image cannot exist in thin air without a screen to catch it.
misconception_label: MISC-OPT-002: Screen Reification (Image Exists Only on Screen)
evidence_rationale: Believes a real image is a physical drawing that only exists if a physical screen is present to capture it; does not understand that rays intersect in space forming an aerial image.

multimodal_context.diagram_description: Convex lens forming real image in air. Cardboard screen is removed, showing rays still converge at the focal plane.
whiteboard_commands: write_equation('Rays converge in space: aerial image exists independently of screen')

topic_concept: Virtual Images & Mirrors
question_text: An object is placed at distance 20 cm in front of a flat plane mirror. Do actual light rays pass through the mirror to form the virtual image?
correct_answer_and_steps: No light rays actually pass through or intersect behind the mirror. Reflected rays diverge into the eye, and the human visual cortex projects them straight backward. Virtual images are formed by the apparent intersection of backward ray extensions, with zero physical light energy behind the mirror.
student_response: Light rays penetrate through the mirror glass and physically focus 20 cm behind the surface.
misconception_label: MISC-OPT-003: Virtual Image Ray Convergence Fallacy
evidence_rationale: Believes virtual images behind a mirror or lens are formed by real physical light rays that penetrate the glass and intersect behind the surface.

multimodal_context.diagram_description: Plane mirror reflecting light into eye, with dotted construction lines showing virtual image behind mirror.
whiteboard_commands: write_equation('No light energy behind mirror; virtual intersection only')

topic_concept: New Cartesian Sign Convention and Mirror/Lens Formulae
question_text: An object is placed at a distance of 50 cm in front of a concave mirror of focal length 25 cm. Using the New Cartesian Sign Convention, determine the image distance v.
correct_answer_and_steps: Under New Cartesian Sign Convention: pole is origin, incident direction is positive. Object is in front: u = -{u} cm. Concave mirror focus is in front: f = -{f} cm. 1/v = 1/f - 1/u = -1/{f} - (-1/{u}). Image is real, inverted, at v = -{cor_val} cm in front of mirror.
student_response: 1/v = 1/25 - 1/50 giving positive v, because the object is in front of the mirror.
evidence_rationale: Treats distances as absolute scalar magnitudes; treats object distance u as positive or forgets that concave mirror focal length is negative.

topic_concept: Refraction through a Rectangular Glass Slab
question_text: Light passes through a flat rectangular glass block of thickness 12 cm. Does the ray exit permanently bent at an angle or parallel to its original path?
correct_answer_and_steps: The emergent ray is parallel to the incident ray (angle of emergence e equals angle of incidence i: e = i). The ray undergoes only a lateral displacement (sideways shift), not an angular deviation, because the opposing refracting surfaces are strictly parallel.
student_response: The ray leaves at a sharp angle to its original direction due to refraction at both surfaces.
misconception_label: MISC-OPT-005: Glass Slab Angular Deviation Fallacy
evidence_rationale: Believes light emerging from a rectangular glass slab is permanently bent at an angle, confusing lateral displacement with angular deviation (prism behavior).

curriculum_chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
topic_concept: Defects of Vision and Their Correction
question_text: An eye examination shows that parallel rays from infinity focus in front of the retina at 100 cm. Which spherical lens will correct this defect?
correct_answer_and_steps: The defect is Myopia (near-sightedness). The eye lens is too converging (or eyeball is elongated), causing distant rays to focus IN FRONT of the retina. A concave (diverging) lens is required to diverge the rays so they focus sharply on the retina.
student_response: The person has hypermetropia and needs a concave lens to push the focus back.
evidence_rationale: Inverts corrective lenses; prescribes convex lens for myopia (short-sightedness) or concave lens for hypermetropia.

multimodal_context.diagram_description: Myopic eye forming image in front of retina, with concave corrective lens diverging rays to focus exactly on retina.
whiteboard_commands: write_equation('Myopia: Eye is too converging => Correct with Diverging (Concave) Lens')

curriculum_chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
topic_concept: Refraction of Light Through a Prism & Dispersion
question_text: A narrow beam of white light passes through a triangular glass prism. Which constituent color undergoes the greatest deviation from its original path?
correct_answer_and_steps: Violet light undergoes the greatest deviation. In glass, refractive index depends on wavelength (Cauchy's relation: n_violet > n_red). Red light travels fastest (v = c/n) and deviates least; violet travels slowest and bends most towards the prism base.
student_response: Red light is deviated the most because red has the strongest and most intense color energy.
misconception_label: MISC-EYE-002: Prism Dispersion Speed and Deviation Inversion
evidence_rationale: Believes red light is deflected most or that red travels slowest in glass, inverting the Cauchy dispersion relation.

multimodal_context.diagram_description: Equilateral glass prism with white light incident. Red refracts least (top of band), Violet refracts most (bottom of band).
whiteboard_commands: write_equation('v_red > v_violet  =>  n_violet > n_red  =>  Violet deviates most')

curriculum_chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
topic_concept: Atmospheric Refraction (Twinkling of Stars)
question_text: Astronauts on the Moon do not observe star twinkling. Why do stars appear to twinkle only from Earth's surface?
correct_answer_and_steps: Twinkling is caused by atmospheric refraction through turbulent, continuously shifting air layers with fluctuating temperatures and refractive indices. Because stars are distant point sources, small refractive deflections cause noticeable wavering in apparent position and brightness. Planets are extended sources, so point fluctuations average out.
student_response: Stars twinkle because nuclear explosions on the star surface turn the light on and off rapidly.
misconception_label: MISC-EYE-003: Star Twinkling Emission Artifact Fallacy
evidence_rationale: Believes stars twinkle because of physical flickering, burning bursts, or cloud obstruction, rather than atmospheric refraction of point sources.

multimodal_context.diagram_description: Light from distant star passing through turbulent atmospheric layers of varying density into observer's eye.
whiteboard_commands: write_equation('Apparent position & brightness waver due to fluctuating air refractive index')

topic_concept: Electric Current in Series Circuits (Conservation of Charge)
question_text: Two identical bulbs B1 and B2 are connected in series with a 6V battery. An ammeter A1 measures current entering B1, and A2 measures current leaving B2. How do the ammeter readings compare?
correct_answer_and_steps: A1 = A2 (current is strictly identical at every point in a series circuit). Electric charge is conserved; electrons cannot accumulate, leak, or be destroyed in a closed loop. Bulbs consume electric potential ENERGY (which converts to heat and light), NOT electric current or electric charge.
student_response: A1 > A2 because bulb B1 consumes some of the electric current to glow, leaving less for A2.
evidence_rationale: Believes electric current is consumed or attenuated by circuit elements like resistors and bulbs as it circulates.

multimodal_context.diagram_description: Series circuit with 6V battery and two identical bulbs. Three ammeters A1, A2, A3 are placed before, between, and after the bulbs.
whiteboard_commands: write_equation('Conservation of Charge: I_in = I_out  =>  A1 = A2 = A3')
write_equation('Current is NOT consumed; only electric potential energy drops')

topic_concept: Parallel Circuits and Source Potential Difference
question_text: A bulb B1 is connected alone across a 12V car battery. An identical bulb B2 is now connected in parallel with B1. How does the brightness of B1 change?
correct_answer_and_steps: Brightness of B1 is UNCHANGED. The battery maintains a constant potential difference V across each parallel branch (V1 = V2 = V). Current in branch 1 remains I1 = V/R. Adding branch 2 lowers the total equivalent resistance (R_eq = R/2), so the battery supplies TWICE the total current (I_total = 2I).

evidence_rationale: Believes a battery produces a fixed constant total current regardless of what external resistance network is connected.

evidence_rationale: Overgeneralizes series addition to parallel circuits, believing adding resistors in parallel increases the total equivalent resistance (R_eq = R1 + R2).

topic_concept: Joule Heating and Electric Power in Parallel vs Series
question_text: Two electric bulbs rated 60 W and 100 W (both at 220 V) are connected in parallel to a 220 V supply. Which bulb has lower resistance and which glows brighter?
correct_answer_and_steps: In parallel, voltage V is constant across both branches. By P = V^2 / R, electric power is inversely proportional to resistance. The smaller resistance draws more current (I = V/R) and dissipates MORE power, glowing brighter.
student_response: The 20 ohm resistor produces more heat because P = I^2 * R, so higher resistance always means more power dissipated.
misconception_label: MISC-ELEC-006: Power Formula Mis-selection in Parallel vs Series
evidence_rationale: Blindly applies P = I^2*R to parallel circuits where V is constant, wrongly concluding that higher resistance produces more heat in parallel.

topic_concept: Nature of Magnetic Poles vs Electrostatic Charges
question_text: A stationary electron is placed at rest near the North pole of a strong permanent bar magnet. What is the magnitude of the magnetic force exerted on the electron?
correct_answer_and_steps: Zero force. The magnetic force on a charged particle is given by the Lorentz force equation F = q * (v x B) = q * v * B * sin(theta). When the charge is stationary (velocity v = 0), the magnetic force is strictly zero. Magnetic poles are dipoles arising from moving charges/spins, not electrostatic monopoles.
student_response: A strong magnetic pole always attracts stationary electric charges just like a charged balloon.
misconception_label: MISC-MAG-001: Magnetic Pole = Electrostatic Charge Equivalence Fallacy
evidence_rationale: Conflates magnetic poles with electrostatic charges, believing North poles are positively charged and attract stationary electrons.

topic_concept: Properties of Magnetic Field Lines
question_text: Why is it impossible for magnetic lines of force to intersect at any point in a magnetic field?
correct_answer_and_steps: No two magnetic field lines can ever cross each other. If they did, a magnetic compass placed at the point of intersection would have to point in two different directions at the same instant, which is physically impossible. The net magnetic field vector at any point has a single unique direction.
student_response: Lines intersect at the neutral point between opposing magnetic poles.
evidence_rationale: Believes magnetic field lines can intersect or cross each other where fields are strong or between two opposing magnets.

topic_concept: Electromagnetic Induction and Faraday's Law
question_text: A wire coil with 200 loops sits motionless inside a steady non-changing magnetic field. Does a galvanometer connected to it deflect?
correct_answer_and_steps: No EMF is induced (EMF = 0 V). Faraday's Law states EMF = -N * dPhi/dt. A constant (non-changing) magnetic field produces zero rate of change of magnetic flux (dPhi/dt = 0), so induced EMF is strictly zero.
student_response: The coil experiences an EMF proportional to field strength times turns = 1000 V.
misconception_label: MISC-MAG-006: Static Field Induces Constant EMF Fallacy
evidence_rationale: Believes that a static (non-changing) magnetic field inside a coil continuously induces an EMF, not realizing that only a changing magnetic flux induces an EMF.

correct_answer_and_steps: No EMF is induced (EMF = 0 V). Faraday's Law states EMF = -N * dPhi/dt. A constant (non-changing) magnetic field produces zero rate of change of magnetic flux (dPhi/dt = 0), so induced EMF is strictly zero.
student_response: Yes, a steady EMF of 200 x 5 = 1000 V is induced because the field acts continuously on the coil.
misconception_label: MISC-MAG-006: Static Field Induces Constant EMF Fallacy
evidence_rationale: Believes that a static (non-changing) magnetic field inside a coil continuously induces an EMF, not realizing that only a changing magnetic flux induces an EMF.

topic_concept: Acceleration vs Constant Velocity
question_text: A high-speed train travels along a straight track at a steady, uniform velocity of 30 m/s for 10 seconds. What is the acceleration of the train during this time?
correct_answer_and_steps: Acceleration is 0 m/s^2. Acceleration is the RATE OF CHANGE of velocity: a = (v - u) / t. Because velocity is constant and direction is unchanged, delta v = 0, so acceleration is strictly zero regardless of how high the speed is.
student_response: Acceleration is 30 m/s^2 because the train is moving very fast at 30 m/s.
evidence_rationale: Equates high speed with high acceleration; believes a vehicle moving at high constant speed must have large acceleration.

multimodal_context.diagram_description: Velocity-time graph showing horizontal line for constant velocity v = 20 m/s. Slope a = dv/dt = 0.
whiteboard_commands: write_equation('Acceleration = Change in Velocity / Time = (v - u) / t')
write_equation('Since v = u = 20 m/s: a = (20 - 20) / 10 = 0 m/s^2')
write_equation('High Speed does NOT equal High Acceleration!')

topic_concept: Newton's Third Law (Action and Reaction)
question_text: A horse pulls a cart forward. By Newton's Third Law, the cart pulls the horse backward with an equal and opposite force. Why doesn't the system remain stationary if the forces are equal and opposite?
correct_answer_and_steps: Action and reaction forces never cancel each other because they ACT ON TWO DIFFERENT BODIES. The forward action force acts ON THE CART, while the backward reaction force acts ON THE HORSE. An object's acceleration depends solely on the net external force acting on THAT specific body.
student_response: Action and reaction balance each other on the cart, so friction has to break the tie.
evidence_rationale: Believes action and reaction forces cancel each other out on the same body, preventing acceleration from occurring.

multimodal_context.diagram_description: Horse pulling a cart. Action force is exerted on cart; reaction force is exerted on horse. Because they act on different bodies, they do not cancel.

topic_concept: Work Done by Force: Direction Dependence
question_text: A porter carries a 25 kg bag on his head and walks horizontally for 25 m. How much work is done by the vertical holding force he exerts?
correct_answer_and_steps: W = F * d * cos(theta). When force is perpendicular to displacement (theta = 90 deg), W = F * d * cos(90 deg) = 0 J. No work is done by a force perpendicular to the direction of motion.
student_response: Force of 25 N for 25 m always gives 250 J of work done.
misconception_label: MISC-WRK-001: Work Equals Force Times Distance Regardless of Direction
evidence_rationale: Applies W = F * d without considering the angle between force and displacement; believes work is done whenever force is applied even if perpendicular to motion.

correct_answer_and_steps: W = F * d * cos(theta). When force is perpendicular to displacement (theta = 90 deg), W = F * d * cos(90 deg) = 0 J. No work is done by a force perpendicular to the direction of motion.
student_response: Force of 25 N for 25 m always gives 250 J of work done.
misconception_label: MISC-WRK-001: Work Equals Force Times Distance Regardless of Direction
evidence_rationale: Applies W = F * d without considering the angle between force and displacement; believes work is done whenever force is applied even if perpendicular to motion.

topic_concept: Law of Conservation of Momentum
question_text: A 3 kg ball moving at 3 m/s collides head-on with an identical stationary ball. Ball 1 stops. What is the velocity of ball 2?
correct_answer_and_steps: By conservation of momentum: p_before = p_after. m*v + 0 = 0 + m*v2, so v2 = v. The second ball moves forward at the same speed ({v} m/s) the first ball originally possessed.
student_response: Ball 1 at rest means total momentum becomes zero; ball 2 remains at rest.
misconception_label: MISC-MOM-001: Momentum Not Conserved When Object Stops
evidence_rationale: Believes momentum is destroyed or disappears when one object stops in a collision, rather than being transferred to another body.
